text: What is NYT Connections puzzle? A daily word-grouping game from The New York Tim. The NYT Connections puzzle is a daily word-grouping game published by The New York Times Games team, in which players sort 16 words into four hidden groups of four. A new puzzle is released at midnight in each player's time zone, and a companion page with hints and answers follows it.. The NYT Connections hints and answers were posted for the Nov. 10 puzzle, and a companion page for the Nov. 7 Sports Edition also drew readers searching for hints.. Each category is rated by difficulty, with the easiest group marked in yellow and the hardest in purple. Players click or tap a level to reveal one word from that category as a hint. The Times says its testers solve each puzzle in advance and rate it out of 5, and players can post their own grids in the comments to compare scores. The companion page is dated by Eastern Standard Time, so two companion pages are live each day. If a reader lands on the wrong one, the page advises checking the puzzle number and finding the matching companion. The Nov. 10 puzzle is numbered #1248 on the companion page. A separate Sports Edition is also published. For the Nov. 7 Sports Edition, numbered #775, the theme was football defensive statistics, and the hint page noted that solving it helps with both American and European football knowledge.

What does purple mean in Connections? Hardest group in NYT puzzle. In the New York Times Connections puzzle, purple is the color of the hardest category. Each puzzle has four groups of four words, colored yellow, green, blue and purple, from simplest to most difficult. Purple marks the group that is hardest to find.. Its hints were given before the full answers, so players can check a clue first.
